Subject: Re: CPAN.pm -> 1.9204

>>>>> On Tue, 13 Nov 2007 07:19:59 +0000, "H.Merijn Brand"  said:

 >> > I'm quite happy with the default, so I won't change the sites.
 >> 
 >> THIS is a bug I can't fix! You're not supposed to keep the default
 >> sites, you're supposed to choose topologically optimal download sites.
 >> Choose a site or three, call mkmyconfig once and you're done forever
 >> with this question.

  > Maybe I can quote Wendy and Johan on this. Not their words, but this
  > is a place where the end-user could use a (good) GUI.

Yes.

  > I also know
  > that this is a chicken-egg problem. A GUI in perl could use Tk or Wx
  > but neither is installed by default (unless you're using ActivePerl
  > on Win32 e.g).

Yes.

  > It's not that I am not willing to change the default, but it is more
  > work to do it than it will save me time.

Depends. It's about latency multiplied by number of downloads vs. a
one time configuration step. People with extremely reliable and fast
internet connections certainly can afford your position.

  > And introducing this question
  > is IMHO not the right incentive to make me change the defaults.

It seem you misunderstand the reason why it is there. The question is
not about parental control, it was introduced because there was demand
based on the fact that the software must give the user the right to
decide about connections to the internet *at least* once. When a user
specifies his own URLs, then this question is not needed anymore. But
before that there are plenty of reasons why a user does not want me to
connect anywhere.

I failed to understand that people do not understand this intent.
Sorry for that.

  > First time through it could ask me, like many browsers do on some
  > sites, if I want to have the option to never ask this question again.

I got it now. I simply did not expect that any user would ever behave
like you do. Thanks for explaining it to me. I simply counted on
people to elect their neighborhood or intranet as the first choice for
downloading. So you have answered my question: apparently a config
variable will work for you.

It's now in my repository as rev. 2448. Hope this fits well.

 >> >> As a quick workaround: at the moment you should be able to use
 >> >> undocumented (and untested)
 >> >> 
 >> >> perl -MCPAN -e '$CPAN::FTP::connect_to_internet_ok=1; shell'
 >> 
 >> > That is a *lot* of typing when you're used to just
 >> 
 >> > # cpan Net::FTP
 >> 
 >> Ah, I thought you want a solution in a scripted environment. For
 >> interactive use the solution is to choose your site.

  > In a scripting environment, I can indeed use a rule like above. I
  > only have to type that once. In the script. Just like I tend to
  > have to use $Data::Dumper::Sortkeys = 1; all the time, as it makes
  > searching through huge data structures a lot easier.

 >> >> I'm open to your suggestions which solution shall be the one to be
 >> >> implemented and documented as the official one.
 >> 
 >> > an environment variable would do, I've got many of those already :)
 >> 
 >> > And as I try to keep some boxes more or less on the bleeding edge of
 >> > development, I do use cpan a lot.
 >> 
 >> Thankyou. I'm willing to help but I do not understand why you're
 >> refusing to change sites.

  > It is not a case of `refusing'. It worked. I'm happy with the way it
  > works, and never felt a compelling reason to change the default. And
  > if I have to change it, I have to change it on at least 8 boxes.

Shiver.

  > Laziness, isn't that one of my good virtues?

You mean the quality that makes you go to great effort to reduce
overall energy expenditure?-)

-- 
andreas
